slides.kicker: Case 01 · Boss of the SOC v1
slides.title: A defaced website. 45 minutes. I traced each step in Splunk.
slides.sub: Web, Sysmon, Windows and firewall logs in one timeline. Then a detection for the next one.

slides.title: The alert: the website shows a defacement page
bullets: **H1:** an admin changed the page. Expect an internal IP and no attack before it.
**H2:** an outsider got in. Expect attack attempts from an external IP, then a request that works.

slides.title: 412 passwords, then a browser
body: A Python script brute-forced the Joomla admin login and hit `batman` at 21:46:33.
92 seconds later, Internet Explorer on a **second IP** logged in with it.

slides.title: The firewall saw it and let it through
body: 2 seconds later: "Upload successful" for `3791.exe` and the web shell `agent.php`.

slides.title: 17 commands through a web shell
body: Sysmon shows `php-cgi.exe` starting `cmd.exe` 17 times: a test `echo`, `dir`, then `3791.exe`, then two `move` commands.

slides.title: A reverse shell the firewall allowed
The download I almost missed
body: My field search on `src_ip` and `dest_ip` found two failed downloads on port 1337.
The third one worked, but its event had **no IPs and no URL**. A plain keyword search for `1337` found it.

slides.title: The detection: a web server should not start a shell
body: On BOTS v1: 17 events, one alert row for `we1149srv`. Before the attack: 0.

slides.title: Verdict: true positive, H2. Escalated as Critical.
bullets: **First action** in my handover note: switch the firewall profile from monitor to block
**Isolate** we1149srv and block both attacker IPs
**Reset** the Joomla admin password and add MFA
**Egress filtering:** a web server has no reason to call out on 3791 or 1337

slides.title: What I took from it
bullets: An event with empty fields is invisible to a field search. Search a plain keyword before you write "not in the logs".
Three log sources agreed within 1 to 2 seconds. That is what high confidence looks like.
Monitor mode detects. It does not protect.
